criteria: Paper 1: gives accurate, specific AO1 detail; judges source usefulness using content and provenance against the stated enquiry; explains similarity/difference and causation with developed reasoning; the Whitechapel extended judgement weighs stimulus and own points to a supported conclusion with acceptable SPaG

Paper 2: explains consequences fully; writes a coherent, chronological, analytical narrative connecting events; explains importance with developed reasoning for the two chosen sub-questions; the British depth study extended judgement weighs stimulus and own points to a supported conclusion

Paper 3: draws two supported inferences from the source; explains causation fully for the chosen topic; judges source usefulness using content and provenance; accurately identifies and explains how and why the two interpretations differ; the extended interpretation judgement uses own knowledge to test the interpretation and reaches a supported conclusion with acceptable SPaG
Across all three papers, uses accurate dates, names and specialist historical terminology (deterrence, retribution, social crime, causation, provenance, interpretation) consistently and correctly
exam_rubric.pass_threshold: A pass is a Grade-4-standard performance across all three papers combined: accurate, well-selected AO1 knowledge; developed AO2 causation, change/continuity, similarity/difference and significance analysis; AO3 source usefulness judgements grounded in content and provenance; and, on Paper 3, AO4 interpretation analysis reaching a supported judgement; extended answers show a clear, evidenced line of reasoning and a stated overall judgement where the question asks for one, with acceptable SPaG on the two designated questions.
